text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday, prepared for Reuters by the Estonian news agency ETA. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The government supported a law on customs tariffs, which may lead to protective tariffs.
- Parliament approved the law on alcohol excise, which increases beer excise rates.

- State-owned company Ookean used to have $600 million worth of property five years ago but the firm is now in debt. 57 ships, buildings, workshops and $100 million in Russian banks has disappeared. The daily is to publish a series of articles about the disappearance of state property.
- Prime minister Mart Siimann met Swedish counterpart Goran Persson during a visit to Sweden.
- The Russian foreign ministry claims that the border agreement text agreed upon last November is not the definitive one and accuses Estonia of causing delays.
- The repair of the premier's car, Mercedes-Benz E420, which was damaged in a collision with the security detail's car last week, will cost 10,000 kroons.
- World-famous sextet The King's Singers are performing in Estonia.
- The absence of a border agreement with Russia need not prevent Estonia's admission to the EU, Foreign Minister Toomas Hendrik Ilves said.
- European Commissioner Hans van den Broek recommended that Estonia strengthen its public sector and its bureaucracy to guarantee the implementation of European laws.
- The state inspection has declared its report on the Bank of Estonia secret.
- Officials consider the Tallinn-Helsinki railway tunnel an insane idea and predict that it could be launched in 20 years at the earliest.
